identity.title: Melena on digital rectal exam, or reported black tarry stool / hematemesis

technique.how: Ask specifically about black, tarry, sticky, foul-smelling stool and about vomiting blood or coffee-ground material, including timing and iron/bismuth use. Perform a digital rectal examination with the patient in left lateral position and inspect the stool on the glove: melena is black, tarry, and glistening (distinct from dark formed stool); note red blood or clots.
technique.prerequisites: Patient consent and privacy; a chaperone per local policy.
technique.contraindications: Relative: severe neutropenia, recent anorectal surgery, or anal fissure/pain (obtain stool sample by other means).

interpretation.positive_finding: Melenic stool on examination strongly favours an upper GI source (LR 25); a patient-reported history of melena raises the likelihood of UGIB about 5-fold.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of melena or hematemesis does not exclude UGIB (brisk bleeds may present with hematochezia); blood clots in the stool make UGIB much less likely (LR 0.05).
interpretation.pitfalls: Iron, bismuth, charcoal, and some foods blacken stool without the tarry sheen; melena requires roughly 50-100 mL of blood and may lag hours behind bleeding onset, and occult-blood testing of dark stool is not a substitute for inspection. Melena reflects source, not severity - use tachycardia, hemoglobin, and the Blatchford score for severity.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as UGIB (IV access, type and screen, PPI, GI consult, Blatchford score for urgency); clots or bright red blood shift work-up toward a lower GI source.

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding vs lower GI bleeding (finding: melenic stool on examination)
estimates.population: Adults admitted or evaluated in EDs with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (8 studies distinguishing UGIB from LGIB; N = 1776)

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding vs lower GI bleeding (finding: patient-reported history of melena; LR range 5.1-5.9 across studies, lower bound entered)
estimates.population: Adults admitted or evaluated in EDs with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (8 studies distinguishing UGIB from LGIB; N = 1776)
estimates.quote: a patient-reported history of melena (LR range, 5.1-5.9)

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding vs lower GI bleeding (finding: blood clots in stool, presence; LR of the finding's presence)
estimates.population: Adults admitted or evaluated in EDs with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (8 studies distinguishing UGIB from LGIB; N = 1776)
estimates.quote: the presence of blood clots in stool (LR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.38) decreases the likelihood of a UGIB

sources.citation: Srygley FD, Gerardo CJ, Tran T, Fisher DA. Does this patient have a severe upper gastrointestinal bleed? JAMA. 2012;307(10):1072-1079.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of melena to dismiss GI bleeding in a syncopal, hypotensive, or anemic patient on anticoagulants or with cirrhosis; do not use melena to judge severity.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Melena or hematemesis with tachycardia, hypotension, hemoglobin <8 g/dL, or cirrhosis (possible variceal bleed) needs urgent resuscitation, transfusion planning, and emergent endoscopy.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: The LR for melenic stool on examination comes from a small number of patients (95% CI 4-174); history of melena is reported as a range across studies rather than a pooled value.

extraction_notes: All numbers are from the Srygley 2012 JAMA RCE abstract (JAMA, no PMC full text); sensitivities and specificities for melena are in the article tables, which were not accessible, so only LRs are entered. History of melena is reported as an LR range (5.1-5.9) not a pooled point estimate; the lower bound 5.1 is entered as the value with no CI, and the range is stated in target_condition. Blood clots in stool is entered with the LR of the finding's presence (0.05) in lr_positive, since it is a rule-out for UGIB when present. Hematemesis-specific LRs were not in the abstract. Verifier: check Srygley Table 2 for melena sensitivity/specificity and hematemesis LR.
